name: Guardian genius crossword No 277
preamble: The puzzle is a safe. Solvers must reveal its contents using four dials, applying each to a quarter of the clues. Dial by dial in clue order, certain letters give a property of 23 cells to be highlighted: Dial 1 clues: extra letter indicated by wordplay Dial 2 clues: first letter of an extra word Dial 3 clues: letter omitted by wordplay Dial 4 clues (normal): clue’s first letter

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Almost limitlessly whole, with zero mass, as is Arnold Rimmer

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundary letters, so only the inside of the word stays

blocks.note: the word with its first and last letters removed
O looks like the figure zero
the gram is a unit of mass
the extra word of a Dial 2 clue; its A is the first letter of that dial's run

explanation.surface: A science-fiction fan describes a television character as a near-perfect projection with no physical weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' seems to soften 'limitlessly whole', but it is this Dial 2 clue's extra word. Arnold Rimmer is the character in the sitcom Red Dwarf who exists only as a projected image.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimmer is the dead crewman revived on Red Dwarf as a three-dimensional light projection, an example of such an image.

clue.text: Stuck moving forward at first, eventually was busily active

indicators.note: the opening letter moves on one step through the alphabet, swapping it for the next

blocks.note: something gummed is stuck down
the extra word of a Dial 2 clue; its E is fifth in that dial's run

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a rut finally got going and became busy.
explanation.walkthrough: G moves forward one place in the alphabet to H.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that hums is buzzing with activity, so it hummed when it was busy and lively.

clue.text: Boiling heat? Linger, taking more time

indicators.note: boiling water churns about, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: On a sweltering day someone advises staying around longer.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAT and LINGER hold ten letters for a nine-letter answer; the spare A is fifth in the Dial 1 run.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthier means longer in duration, so a lengthier task is one that lasts more hours.

clue.text: Punch with seething rage on top part of car

indicators.note: seething liquid is agitated, so these letters are churned around

blocks.note: taken as written
to box is to punch

explanation.surface: An angry driver thumps the roof of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal Dial 4 clue; its P is fifth in that dial's run. In a down clue 'on top' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The gearbox is the housing for a car's gears, a component of the transmission.

clue.text: Tools to dispose of board

blocks.note: to axe something is to get rid of it
a board of directors is made up of the heads of a company

explanation.surface: Equipment for getting rid of a plank of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal Dial 4 clue; its T is sixth in that dial's run.
explanation.definitionFit: Axeheads are the metal blades of axes, the working parts of these implements.

clue.text: Fellow welcomed by criminals lacking basis of moral fibre

indicators.note: guests who are welcomed are taken in, so the group wraps round the newcomer
the basis of a word is where it starts, its opening letter
lacking something means being without it, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: the letter the wordplay leaves out in this Dial 3 clue, first of that dial's run
the Mafia is a criminal organisation
F is the abbreviation for fellow
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man joins a gang of crooks who have no moral backbone.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds MAFFIA and drops its M, leaving AFFIA; the missing R is the Dial 3 letter. 'Moral fibre' reads as one phrase, but fibre alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is the soft fibre stripped from palm leaves and used for weaving baskets, mats and hats.

clue.text: A perfectly reasonable, intrinsically rational inference – from what goes before?

blocks.note: its first letter
its first letter
its first letter
its first letter
the letter the wordplay leaves out in this Dial 3 clue, fifth of that dial's run
its first letter
its first letter

explanation.surface: A philosopher describes reasoning that follows logically from premises already given.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer comes from what goes before: the initials of the six words ahead of the dash spell APRIRI, missing the O that is the Dial 3 letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori is Latin for from the earlier, reasoning from prior principles rather than experience.

clue.text: Stood opposite transport café

indicators.note: transported things are carried off elsewhere, so these letters are moved into new places

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter the wordplay leaves out in this Dial 3 clue, sixth of that dial's run

explanation.surface: A transport café stood across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: A transport café is a British roadside diner for lorry drivers; here 'transport' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that faced a building stood across from it, looking towards it.

clue.text: Get up, Ed - and, in getting up, reveal poison

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means rising, read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to arise is to get up
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone urges Ed to rise and, while dressing, uncover a toxin.
explanation.walkthrough: ARISE then NIDE gives one letter too many; the spare I is sixth in the Dial 1 run.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenide is a compound of arsenic with another element, and many are highly toxic.

clue.text: Fast trumpet concerto’s closing slow passage

indicators.note: the closing part of a word is its very end, its final letter

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
its final letter
the extra word of a Dial 2 clue; its T is sixth in that dial's run

explanation.surface: A quick trumpet concerto ends with a slow section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like a tempo set against 'slow', but it is the period of fasting; 'trumpet' is the extra word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the Italian musical direction for a slow tempo, and names a movement played that way.

clue.text: Style of art seen after sculpting metal

indicators.note: sculpting reshapes material into a new form, so these letters are remodelled

blocks.note: manga is the Japanese comic-book art style
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gallery note says a style of art was spotted after a sculptor worked in metal.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal Dial 4 clue; its first letter S begins that dial's run.
explanation.definitionFit: Manganese is a hard grey metallic element used chiefly in making steel alloys.

clue.text: Rents shelves

blocks.note: rents are tears or splits, as are cracks

explanation.walkthrough: This is a Dial 1 clue: the wordplay gives one letter too many, and the spare C of CRACKS is the first letter of that dial's run. It looks like a double definition with 'rents' as payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Racks are frames or stands of shelving on which things are stored or displayed.

clue.text: In the end, people want a kebab which’ll be possible to swallow

indicators.note: the end of each word is its final letter, so those closing letters are collected

blocks.note: its closing letter
the letter the wordplay leaves out in this Dial 3 clue, second of that dial's run
its closing letter
a one-letter word is its own last letter
its closing letter
its closing letter, ignoring the apostrophe
its closing letter

explanation.surface: Late at night, everyone fancies a kebab that will go down easily.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of people want a kebab which'll be give ETABLE; the A that the wordplay misses is the Dial 3 letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eatable is fit to be eaten, so it can be put in the mouth and got down.

clue.text: Trampled and thumped mercilessly in the head by two short men

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: its first letter
two names shortened, Rodney and Dennis, cut to their first three letters
the extra word of a Dial 2 clue; its M is second in that dial's run

explanation.surface: Someone was trodden underfoot and beaten savagely about the head by a pair of small men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mercilessly' feels essential to the beating, but it is the extra word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trodden is the past participle of tread, meaning crushed or flattened underfoot by walking.

clue.text: Chinese No. 1 visiting electronic component compound

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside the place visited, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a diode is a component that lets current flow one way
Xi Jinping is China's leader

explanation.surface: China's top man drops in on a maker of electronic parts.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal Dial 4 clue; its first letter C is second in that dial's run.
explanation.definitionFit: A dioxide is a chemical compound whose molecules contain two oxygen atoms, as carbon dioxide does.

clue.text: Burned some King Edwards

blocks.note: the letter the wordplay leaves out in this Dial 3 clue, third of that dial's run
says that only part of the next words is used, a run of letters from inside them
the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A cook has scorched a batch of potatoes; King Edwards are a popular British potato variety.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run INGED lacks the S at the start, which is the Dial 3 letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Singed means scorched lightly on the surface, a mild form of burning.

clue.text: Beau’s legs toned with exercise - no working out needed

indicators.note: exercise works the body over, so these letters are pummelled into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
the extra word of a Dial 2 clue; its T is seventh in that dial's run

explanation.surface: A boyfriend's legs got shapely through exercise, with no gym workout required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working out' suggests a gym session, but here it means calculation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something guessable can be arrived at by intuition, without any reasoning or calculation.

clue.text: I advanced to south of island in Ian Smith’s land

blocks.note: Rhodes is a Greek island
taken as written
A is short for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A traveller describes moving to the south of an island in a former African state.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal Dial 4 clue; its I is seventh in that dial's run. In a down entry, south of means placed below.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Smith led the white-minority government of Rhodesia, the former name of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Travelling up Great North Road by electric vehicle, husband exhibits fatal flaw

indicators.note: travelling upwards in a down entry means the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
the letter the wordplay leaves out in this Dial 3 clue, seventh of that dial's run
the Great North Road is the A1, its 1 read as I
trams run on electricity

explanation.surface: A husband heading north by electric car reveals a tragic weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1, the Great North Road, runs from London to Edinburgh. The wordplay makes HMARTIA; the A it misses is the Dial 3 letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamartia is the term from Greek tragedy for the hero's error or defect of character that brings his downfall.

clue.text: Steel core in lead casing for this object

definitions.note: an adverb phrase meaning to this end

indicators.note: the core of something is its centre, so the middle letter is taken
a casing wraps around its contents, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: the lead in a story is its hero
the middle letter of a five-letter word
the letter the wordplay leaves out in this Dial 3 clue, fourth of that dial's run

explanation.surface: An engineer describes a steel core inside a lead sheath, made for this particular item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal beside steel, but it means the leading character. The wordplay makes HEREO; the T it misses is the Dial 3 letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereto is a formal word meaning to this matter or purpose, as in documents attached hereto.

clue.text: Bird, arachnid and insect

blocks.note: the tern is a seabird
mites are tiny arachnids

explanation.surface: A list of three creatures: a bird, a spider-like animal and a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: TERN and MITE give one letter too many; the spare N is seventh in the Dial 1 run.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are social insects that live in colonies and feed on wood.

clue.text: Employer wasted time, passed over everyone

indicators.note: lying over something covers it on both sides here, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: to pass away is to die
all people means everyone
the extra word of a Dial 2 clue; its E is third in that dial's run

explanation.surface: A boss frittered away the day and ignored all the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employer' reads as the subject of the sentence, but it is the extra word.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to linger idly or dawdle, so someone who dallied let time slip by.

clue.text: Generation eschewed speech, inward, vacuous, emotionless and lazy

indicators.note: to eschew something is to shun it, so that word is taken out
vacuous means empty, so the inside is cleared out and only the outer letters remain

blocks.note: language is spoken speech
an age is a generation
its first and last letters
the extra word of a Dial 2 clue; its E is last in that dial's run

explanation.surface: A generation is mocked as inarticulate, inward-looking, empty-headed, cold and idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emotionless' fits the list of insults, but it is the extra word.
explanation.definitionFit: Languid describes someone listless and slow-moving, lacking energy or the will to exert themselves.

clue.text: Thread evenly uncoiling from the end

indicators.note: evenly picks the even-numbered positions, the second, fourth and so on
starting from the end means reading from the last letter back to the first

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
the letter the wordplay leaves out in this Dial 3 clue, last of that dial's run

explanation.surface: A length of yarn unwinds steadily from its end.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters read backwards give NLON; the Y it lacks is the Dial 3 letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic polymer spun into strong fibres, sold as fishing line and sewing yarn.

clue.text: They transport compost: it's dug into the soil

definitions.note: a description: the root grows in earth and is dug up

blocks.note: cars carry people about
compost is rotted matter

explanation.surface: A gardener says barrows carry compost which is worked into the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay has one letter too many; the spare S closes the Dial 1 run, completing the word CONTAINS. 'They transport' reads as the definition's subject, but it is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is a root vegetable that grows below ground and has to be lifted with a fork.

clue.text: __ __ exemplify ‘ruin’?

blocks.note: the two blanks are filled by two words that make the clue a question about an ancient city

explanation.surface: A question asks whether a famous fallen city is the very model of a ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the blanks as 'Does Troy', the city sacked by the Greeks; DOES TROY has one letter too many, and its spare O is second in the Dial 1 run.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy something is to wreck it completely, which is what the verb ruin means.

clue.text: Country east of Cyprus, bright and open to the north

indicators.note: on a map the east is the right-hand side, which in a word is its final letter
heading north in a down entry means going upwards, so the letters run bottom to top

blocks.note: an airy room is bright and open
its final letter

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern nation lying beyond Cyprus is sunny and accessible from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal Dial 4 clue; its C is last in that dial's run. 'Country east of Cyprus' looks like the definition, and true, but only 'Country' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Remembering a name is tricky with this!

definitions.text: Remembering a name is tricky with this!

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward to sort out, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sympathises that names are hard to recall when you suffer from this condition.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal Dial 4 clue; its first letter R is third in that dial's run. The whole clue defines the answer as well as containing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, so with it you would struggle to recall anything, names included.

clue.text: Bad weather in Kent caravan site

blocks.note: Kent is a county in South East England
rain is the bad weather

explanation.surface: Foul weather hits a caravan park in Kent, an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: SE and RAIN make SERAIN, one letter over; the spare N is third in the Dial 1 run. 'Caravan site' suggests holiday parks, but a serai is an inn for camel caravans.
explanation.definitionFit: A serai, short for caravanserai, is an inn with a courtyard where travelling caravans of merchants stop for the night.

clue.text: Have more than one rum - but long, not neat

indicators.note: untidy letters are in disorder, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the extra word of a Dial 2 clue; its L is fourth in that dial's run

explanation.surface: A drinker orders a second rum, a long one, and not neat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' and 'not neat' both suggest a diluted drink, but long is the extra word.
explanation.definitionFit: To outnumber a group is to exceed it in number, having more members or items than it.

clue.text: Years after Christ’s birth, wise men discovered Proverbs

indicators.note: dis-covered means having its cover lifted, so the opening letter is stripped off

blocks.note: Anno Domini marks years counted from the Nativity
sages are wise men

explanation.surface: The Magi turn up soon after the Nativity, but what they found was a book of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal Dial 4 clue; its Y is fourth in that dial's run. 'Proverbs' looks like the biblical book, but it is a plain plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Adages are traditional sayings expressing a common truth, which is what proverbs are.

clue.text: Psychic debunker with screen turned on to max

indicators.note: turned over means churned around, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: James Randi was a stage magician famous for exposing fake psychics
a screening is a test

explanation.surface: A sceptic of the paranormal switches on his television at full volume.
explanation.walkthrough: RANDI and a reshuffled TEST give one letter too many; the spare T is fourth in the Dial 1 run. 'On', as in turned on, means aroused.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy means lustful, sexually aroused, so the superlative is the most aroused anyone can be.
